body.statement: For every admissible balanced pilot-size sequence \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) with \(m/\sqrt n\to0\) or \(m/\sqrt n\to\infty\), including bounded \(m\), positive pilot fractions, and \(N=o(n)\), \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)=\infty.\]
body.justification: Endpoint exclusion is needed to promote the interior expansion from a candidate scale to the unique global pilot scale.
body.gap: First-order oracle equivalence does not compare bounded, vanishing, macroscopic, and nearly all-pilot sequences on one risk scale.
body.consumer: It prevents a planner from exploiting a degenerate pilot or main wave that appears favorable only because the interior approximation was used outside its domain.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform minimax lower bounds for bounded pilots, positive pilot fractions, and nonvanishing main-wave fractions outside the interior expansion.
obligation.obstruction: The corrected one-wave inequality is memberwise unless a common moment envelope is added, and the frozen results contain no first-order comparison showing that arbitrary finite actions cannot beat the raw Gaussian oracle over those endpoint windows.
obligation.attempted: Established the nearly-all-pilot argument conditional on a fixed-member moment envelope and positive full-oracle gain. The other windows require a two-point testing or first-order localization argument not present in the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result:
For a fixed model member with a common conditional second-moment envelope, the corrected one-wave bound implies that the greatest possible contribution of a main wave of size \(N\) to the pooled risk is \(O(N/n^2)\).  Therefore, if
\[
n\,d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\to A(\beta_0)>0,
\]
every sequence with \(N=o(n)\) has excess at least \(A(\beta_0)/(2n)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and its \(n^{3/2}\)-scaled excess diverges.  Bounded-pilot and positive-fraction windows still require a first-order arbitrary-action lower comparison that is not supplied by the frozen assumptions.
